tldr: Exact score-ratio information and risk frontier, strong-region Gaussian inference, and an all-strength honest inversion whose boundary totalization is strong-region adaptive. For a posted-price platform on a preregistered finite product--market support, a sealed independent audit converts the production-code comparison into the pointwise radius \(|D|\le ca\) before outcomes are opened. Exact nullity over the certified interval forces bounded Gaussian--Rademacher scores to be antiperiodic; folding modulo \(4a\) gives the exact exponentially small relevance \(I_a\) and the matching risk \(\Theta\{\min(1,(nI_a)^{-1})\}\) over deterministic pre-analysis exact-null score ratios. The unprojected sine ratio has a uniform Gaussian pivot when \(nI_a\to\infty\). Unconditional exact-null inversion is uniformly asymptotically honest for every triangular \(a_n\), with no strength restriction. The old full-range empty-set fallback remains sharply diagnosed as nonadaptive at a boundary law, whereas the boundary-totalized report preserves all-strength coverage, is \(o_P((nI_a)^{-1/2})\)-Hausdorff equivalent to the guarded Wald interval in the strong region, and has expected diameter at most \(C\min\{2,(nI_a)^{-1/2}\}\). The comparison remains confined to deterministic exact-null score ratios, and no all-estimator or all-confidence-procedure minimax claim is made.
